# DSH Session Matrix

> A panoramic console for multi-Agent sessions in DeepSeek Harness. Watch several sessions and
> subagents running in parallel without switching, see the parent/child Agent graph at a glance,
> and hand work off before compaction drops the details.

DSH Session Matrix is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/) (DSH) that adds
one sidebar entry with two views:

- **Workspace** — a session list plus 1–4 panes, where every pane is a real native conversation
  (DSH's own `conversation.content` factory), not a preview or a mirror. You can type and send in each
  pane; subagent panes are read-only.
- **Agent Graph** — a neural-link graph `workbench → project → main session → subagent`. Edges come from
  the real `parentSession` field, not inferred "same project" guesses. Node colour is distance to the
  compaction point; node size is cumulative usage. Selecting a node re-scopes three modules underneath:
  context composition, cumulative usage and estimated cost, and a session matrix.

It also implements **Agent Handoff**: a protocol-v1 prompt that makes an agent write
`HANDOFF-<timestamp>.md` (goal, progress, key files, rejected approaches, open questions) plus a
takeover message, so work can continue in a fresh session before compaction throws the details away.
The button only copies — it does not send or modify any session.

## When to use it

- You run several sessions and subagents at once and need to see which one is about to compact.
- You hand work between sessions (model switch, next day, after compaction) and want a repeatable
  protocol instead of retyping context.
- You want to know where the tokens went without opening a separate dashboard.

If you only run one session, you do not need this.

## Facts

- Package: `dsh-session-matrix` (npm), display name 会话矩阵工作台 / Session Matrix.
- License: MIT. Runtime dependencies: none. Two source files, no build step.
- Requires DSH `>= 0.2.2-rc.1`, Node `^22.19.0` or `>= 24`.
- Verified on DSH `0.2.2-rc.x`, Windows 11. macOS and Linux are not yet verified on real hardware.
- Cost is CNY: DeepSeek's official price list, peak hours (Beijing time, Mon–Fri 09:00–12:00 and
  14:00–18:00, holidays excluded) at 2×. Non-DeepSeek routes fall back to models.dev in USD.
- Context occupancy uses the provider-reported prompt size, not a character-count estimate.
- Compaction point mirrors the official `dsh-compaction-basic` formula:
  `contextWindow − reservedCompletionTokens − headroomTokens` (headroom defaults to 4096), which is
  788,480 tokens (75.2%) for a 1,048,576 window with 256,000 reserved. An earlier estimate
  (`min(window × 80%, window − output − 64K)`) warned too early and was removed. Watch line = point × 80%,
  critical line = point × 92%. This is a warning only; it does not expand context or stop compaction.
- Handoff advice also counts compactions from `compact-checkpoint` markers in session logs: 0 compactions
  at the critical line = "first approach", still usable, no handoff pushed; 1–2 = advise handoff; 3+ =
  strongly advise. Compaction counts that cannot be read are labelled "unknown", never guessed.

## Not true / not claimed

- It is not a replacement for `dsh-context` (which analyses context far more deeply).
- It is not the only plugin with split views: `dsh-session-grid`, `dsh-multi-session`, and
  `dsh-multi-chat` also do that; some have tabs and tmux-style splitting this plugin lacks.
- It does not price non-DeepSeek models in CNY.
- It has no telemetry and makes no network request except an optional `models.dev` price fetch.
- It does not depend on other plugins. Model names, usage totals and context occupancy come from core
  DSH projections (`modelSelection`, `tokenUsage`, `contextPressure`). Cost prefers the projections'
  peak/off-peak buckets; without them it rebuilds peak/off-peak from per-request timestamps in session
  logs, so the numbers reconcile with `dsh-context` installed. It is an estimate, not a bill.
- Credit: the data shapes and pricing rules follow `dsh-context` (bowenliang123), which is the deeper
  context-analysis plugin in this ecosystem. It is not a code dependency and does not appear in GitHub's
  contributor list, which counts commits only.
